vectors.name: stored-context-is-windowed-to-48-characters
vectors.note: SPEC.md §9: prefix/suffix 'carry up to 48 characters of the neighbour on each side'. Both neighbours here are ~185 characters, so a conforming build stores the LAST 48 of the preceding block and the FIRST 48 of the following one. This is the only category that can catch a producer storing whole neighbour blocks: every resolve vector windows both sides at match time, so a nonconformant producer resolves identically and passes the whole resolve category. Through v1.2 every implementation stored the whole block and this vector is what would have caught it.

Operators can override these retry defaults on a per-partner basis, but every override expires automatically after thirty days so that stale tuning never silently persists in production.

The ingest stage retries failed operations three times.

Each completed run is recorded in the audit log together with the operator name, the affected partner, and the exact timestamp of the change, so the history is always reconstructable.

vectors.name: short-neighbours-are-stored-whole
vectors.note: 48 is a cap, not a fixed width. Neighbours under the limit are stored verbatim, so an implementation that pads, truncates to a fixed length, or normalizes at build time fails here. Storage is raw text; §9's ASCII fold is a matching-time operation.

vectors.name: document-edges-have-empty-context
vectors.note: The first block has no preceding neighbour and the last has no following one, so those sides are the empty string rather than a wrapped or duplicated block. The unmarked middle block contributes no anchor while still serving as both neighbours, which pins that anchors follow markers and context follows position.
